classification.difficultyReason: Requires graphical addition of ordinates across piecewise linear, parabolic and restricted-domain curves, including cancellation, endpoints and turning behaviour.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12, upper-left graph of the 12–15 range
spec.description: Unscaled axes; a rising blue line through the origin and a descending red piecewise line with a shallower right branch. Both component graphs continue at their outer ends.
spec.mathematics: Left component ordinates cancel. On the right, the blue ordinate exceeds the magnitude of the negative red ordinate. Coordinates are internal schematic drawing units, with no numerical givens or ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied component graphs are visible.

answer.worked: For $x<0$, the component ordinates are equal and opposite, so their sum is zero. For $x>0$, subtract the magnitude of the negative red ordinate from the positive blue ordinate. This gives the upward ray shown.

spec.description: Complete solution graph with light dashed components and a solid sum on the negative x-axis, continuing as a rising ray on the right.
spec.mathematics: Pointwise ordinate addition in the same internal coordinate frame as the supplied graph.
spec.answerVisibility: The sum appears only in answer editions.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13, upper-right graph of the 12–15 range
spec.description: Unscaled axes with a rising blue line through the origin and an upward-opening red parabola whose vertex is at the origin. The graphs intersect again in the first quadrant.
spec.mathematics: The plotted parabola and line use internal normalized drawing units to preserve the source shape and intersections. No equations, numerical coordinates or ticks are supplied to students.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied component graphs are visible.

answer.worked: Add the ordinates vertically. At the origin the sum is zero. Immediately to the left, the negative blue ordinate has greater magnitude than the positive red ordinate, so the sum is negative. Farther left the red ordinate dominates, making the sum positive. For $x>0$, both ordinates are positive. Join these points with the upward-opening curve shown.

spec.description: Complete solution graph: an upward-opening sum curve with a minimum below the x-axis to the left of the y-axis, crossing the x-axis at the origin and farther left.
spec.mathematics: The sum is plotted from the component functions in their shared internal drawing frame. Numerical drawing coordinates are not source givens.
spec.answerVisibility: The sum appears only in answer editions.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14, lower-left graph of the 12–15 range
spec.description: Unscaled axes with a descending blue line through the origin and an increasing concave-down red curve beginning on the negative x-axis. The curves cross above the x-axis left of the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: A parametric normalized concave-down curve preserves the visible start, direction and relative placement. It supplies no numerical endpoint or equation to students.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied component graphs are visible.

answer.worked: Use only $x$-values where both graphs exist. At the red curve's left endpoint its ordinate is zero, so the sum equals the positive blue ordinate. Initially the rapidly rising red curve makes the sum rise. As its rise slows, the falling blue line dominates, so the sum turns downward and eventually becomes negative. At the $y$-axis, the blue ordinate is zero, so the sum equals the red ordinate.

spec.description: Complete solution graph with a closed left endpoint above the x-axis, a nearby maximum, and a decreasing right branch crossing the positive x-axis.
spec.mathematics: The sum is derived by ordinate addition in the component graph's internal normalized coordinate frame and is restricted to their common domain.
spec.answerVisibility: The sum and its endpoint marker appear only in answer editions.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 15, lower-right graph of the 12–15 range
spec.description: Unscaled axes with a rising blue line through the origin and a red upper semicircle centred at the origin, ending on the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: The semicircle uses a normalized internal radius solely for drawing. No radius, scale or numerical coordinates are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied component graphs are visible.

answer.worked: Add the semicircle's ordinate to the line's ordinate wherever both exist. At each semicircle endpoint its ordinate is zero, so the sum lies on the line. At the $y$-axis the line contributes zero, so the sum passes through the semicircle's top point. Between the endpoints the sum lies above the line. Its maximum is to the right of the $y$-axis before it falls to the right endpoint.

spec.description: Complete solution graph confined to the semicircle's horizontal span, with closed endpoints on the line, a left x-intercept, and a maximum to the right of the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: The parametric sum adds the line ordinate to the semicircle ordinate in the shared internal coordinate frame. The endpoints are included and no extension beyond the common domain is drawn.
spec.answerVisibility: The sum and endpoint markers appear only in answer editions.
